turns.content: We store Wikipedia page revisions in a MariaDB table `page_rev` and want to answer 'what did the article on X say on 2026-03-01 12:00?'. Should I use system versioning or just a revision table with timestamps?

Short answer: it depends on where the timestamps come from. System-versioned tables (WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING) record row validity from when your database saw the change, not when Wikipedia saved the revision. If you load historical dumps, ROW_START would be your load time, so FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF would give wrong dated answers. For Wikipedia's own revision time I'd propose an explicit `rev_timestamp` column. Which MariaDB version are you on? Proposal for you to approve: add a composite index on (page_id, rev_timestamp) and test the boundary query `rev_timestamp <= '2026-03-01 12:00:00' ORDER BY rev_timestamp DESC LIMIT 1`. I have not run anything.

turns.content: Plan: load Wikipedia dumps into a system-versioned table and answer dated questions with FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF.

Caution: ROW_START reflects when MariaDB changed the row, not Wikipedia's edit time. If you bulk load dumps today, every row starts today and AS OF 2026-03-01 would return nothing or wrong data. Proposal: keep rev_timestamp as a real column for Wikipedia time, and use system versioning only to audit your own corrections. Please confirm how you load data.
We replay each revision in chronological order and set the session clock with SET TIMESTAMP before each insert, so ROW_START matches the Wikipedia time.
